newsitem.title: UK: Briton bets $794 on son, 7, emulating Damon Hill.
newsitem.headline: Briton bets $794 on son, 7, emulating Damon Hill.

text.p: A father inspired by Briton Damon Hill's victory in this year's world Formula One car racing championship has placed a bet on his seven-year-old son emulating the feat which could net him over $750,000.
Airline pilot Philip Martin-Dye, 44, backed his younger child Freddie to the tune of 500 pounds ($794), getting odds of 1,000 to one from bookmakers Ladbrokes.
He said Freddie had been driving a go-kart around a farm close to his southern England home for almost three years now and would shortly be able to take part in races for eight-year-olds.
"He wants to be out driving all time. He loves it so much, he follows all the Grand Prix," he added.
Hill clinched the championship last weekend by winning the final grand prix of the season in Suzuki, Japan, with Freddie watching the event on television and cheering his hero on.

Ladbrokes public relations manager Ed Nicholson said the bet was unusual, but his company had been happy to take it on. "Damon Hill proved that a Brit can do it, and who knows Freddie may be the next British World Champion?," he said.
